question: Should Octopool replace the single caller-token model with the proposed per-client token table and 16-client retention policy in the next release?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, but it changes persistent auth storage, audit attribution, CLI/API output, and session-retention policy, which are product and upgrade choices rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Proceed With Migration
options.body: Accept the per-client token table and 16-client cap after reviewing upgrade proof and release context for existing deployments.

options.title: Narrow Before Merge
options.body: Ask the branch to keep the storage change smaller or more default-compatible until the retention and dashboard semantics are settled.

options.title: Defer Direction
options.body: Pause this PR until a maintainer-sponsored design for caller session identity and retention is agreed.

recommendation.title: Proceed With Migration
recommendation.body: Accept the per-client token table and 16-client cap after reviewing upgrade proof and release context for existing deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main caller/auth feature history and this PR's domain both point to `steipete` as the best owner for the product and upgrade call.
